approvedDeviation: #883 ships the native grant sheet, composed replica reads, and the pin/download engine on the phone, so the Hermes index chunk grows past the #821 7.75 MB ceiling (CI mobile-smoke observed 7,958,356 B iOS / 7,978,937 B Android). Ceiling maxLargestChunkBytes 7750000 → 8220000 (largest observed + ~3% headroom). maxTotalBytes is unchanged. No second copy of kit was added; the growth is the grant/replica/offline work this umbrella bought. Prior: #821.
_comment: Experience budgets for the Expo iOS/Android app (apps/mobile). Perceived latency only. See README.md in this directory for the status vocabulary and the year-3 volume table. Ratcheted tighten-only via PERF_BUDGET_SOURCES.

coldOpenToUsable.volume: device-local replica seeded by the e2e first-run flow (NOT year-3 — see _note)
coldOpenToUsable.probe: tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/cold-start.mjs — PER-LAUNCH cold start (stopApp → launchApp → Home ready marker), 8 launches, reports median and p95. Runs on the nightly mobile-e2e-ios / mobile-e2e-android jobs and on the run-probes-suite path of the per-merge canary.
coldOpenToUsable._note: The pre-existing tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/volume-proof.mjs measures 20 relaunches as ONE wall-clock total, so a single 10 s launch hides inside a 20-launch sum and the number is unreadable as an experience. The new flow reports per-launch statistics. No ceilingMs on first land: an on-device number from a CI simulator has no distribution yet, so the flow gates on the trailing-median drift budget (>1.5x sustained) from its own 30-sample history. The replica volume is also not year-3 yet — docs/mobile-offline.md's 90k figure is an explicitly labelled PROJECTION, not a run. #890 W1 changed WHAT this measures: the lane now installs a release-configuration build with the Hermes bundle embedded, so a launch is a real app start rather than a dev-client bundle fetch from Metro. Every sample recorded before that change was taken against a __DEV__ build and is not comparable — the drift history starts again here.

maxDroppedFramePercent.volume: Photos grid and People directory holding whatever the CI gateway fixture seeded — NOT the declared year-3 90,000 assets / 5,000 contacts. The flow publishes `people rows observed`, a real lower bound it can see, rather than guessing the seeded total.
maxDroppedFramePercent.probe: tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/scroll-frames.mjs — arms apps/mobile's sampler with openLink centraid://perf-frames?ms=6000, confirms testID perf-frame-sampling, flings 8x, then reads testID perf-frame-report and parses `dropped=<number>%`. Contract pinned by apps/mobile/src/lib/perf/frame-sampler.test.ts.

_provenance.attempted: not yet — needs a booted simulator; pending the rebuilt nightly mobile-e2e-ios / mobile-e2e-android jobs and the per-merge mobile-canary lane. #890 W1 is what makes a run possible at all: the sampler was __DEV__-only, so before it the probe could only ever have measured a development build. It is now compiled into a PERF-FLAVORED RELEASE behind EXPO_PUBLIC_CENTRAID_FRAME_PROBE (apps/mobile/src/kit/perf/FrameProbe.tsx), which the device lanes set on the bundling step and a store build never sets.
_provenance.note: maxPercent 50 is a CATASTROPHE bound, NOT observed + headroom, and is labelled so deliberately. Above 50% the list is running at half the display's refresh rate or worse, which is broken on any device and needs no measurement to assert. The real target is 5% (`_intendedMaxPercent`, underscore-prefixed so it is invisible to the ratchet); it is promoted to `maxPercent` only when a real device run against the release artifact produces a distribution, and the 30-sample/1.5x drift gate is what catches a slow walk in the meantime.
_provenance.denominatorCaveat: `dropped` has a PER-DEVICE denominator. The sampler derives the display's true refresh rate from the 10th-percentile inter-frame interval and snaps to 120/90/60/30 Hz, so the flow records `targetHz` beside every percentage. A comparison that drops it reads 60 fps on a 120 Hz ProMotion device as flawless when half the frames are missing.
_provenance.scopeCaveat: JS THREAD ONLY. The sampler counts requestAnimationFrame callbacks, so jank originating on the UI/native thread (a Reanimated worklet, a native image decode) is invisible to it. This is a real frame-drop number for the JS thread, not a compositor-level guarantee.

tapToVisualResponse.probe: NONE TODAY. Same instrumentation blocker as the frame-drop ceiling: Maestro's tap→assert round trip includes its own polling interval (~hundreds of ms), which swamps the signal being measured.

sendToFirstToken.volume: one stub turn against a fixed-delay ACP provider
sendToFirstToken.probe: RIG EXISTS, NO NUMBER YET — and the distinction is the point. The blocker named here until #890 was that the CI gateway had no model provider at all, so no turn could start and nothing could be timed. That is fixed: tests/agent-e2e-mobile/lib/fixed-delay-agent.mjs is a minimal ACP agent that streams its first token after a KNOWN delay, tests/agent-e2e-mobile/lib/ci-gateway.mjs configures it as the Assistant's provider through the registry's `acp` custom-agent kind, and tests/integration-mobile/assistant-provider.integration.test.ts proves that wiring resolves to a launch plan spawning it (importing the prefs the gateway writes rather than a copy, so the two cannot drift). What is still missing is a DEVICE RUN: the flow that taps send and waits for first paint, on hardware this change had none of. Until that runs, `status` stays `unmeasured` — a rig is not a measurement, and promoting this to `measured` on the strength of wiring is the exact move this budget file exists to prevent. When the flow lands, the number to record is `observed − CENTRAID_STUB_FIRST_TOKEN_DELAY_MS` (default 250), which is the dead time this repo owns: the app's send path, the Iroh hop, gateway turn dispatch and the renderer reaching first paint. The gateway-side lower bound on the same interval is already measured in tests/experience-budgets/gateway.json (#842) and excludes every one of those spans.

reconnectToFresh.volume: 50,000 replica rows (declared year-3, docs/mobile-offline.md) + 200 changes committed while backgrounded, then a 200-row newest-first screen page
reconnectToFresh.probe: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.scale.config.ts tests/scale/mobile-reconnect-to-fresh.scale.test.ts (also `bun run test:scale`) — the nightly scale lane rather than the package suite, because this gates on WALL CLOCK and `bun run test` drives 29 turbo tasks across four threads: under that contention the probe read 3,292 ms against this 1,800 ms ceiling while reading 482 ms alone, so the lane's `fileParallelism: false` forked pool is what makes the number mean anything. It drives the production createNativeReplicaSession: bootstrap, AppState 'background' (feed deactivated), server state advances unseen, AppState 'active', then polls the read a Photos/Docs screen issues until every missed change is on the page. The clock starts on the AppState transition and stops when the SCREEN'S read is fresh, not when the delta lands in SQLite.

_provenance.host: linux x64 development container, Node SQLite driver under the production native session
_provenance.note: RE-MEASURED AFTER PUSHDOWN (#883 C3/D1) and tightened from 20,000 ms. The previous entry measured 6,324-8,382 ms and said in as many words that the screen read was the shrinker: every read materialised all 50,000 rows, JSON.parsed each payload and filtered/sorted in JavaScript before the 200-row limit applied. The compiled read plan made that read one SQL statement, and the same probe now resumes to a fresh screen in ~0.5 s — a 15x fall with no change to what is measured. Scope is UNCHANGED and this ceiling must not be read as the whole interval. INCLUDED: the AppState transition, change-feed reactivation, the delta pull loop, applying 200 missed changes, and the 200-row newest-first screen read that has to return them. EXCLUDED: real network RTT (the gateway is an in-process fetch double - the gateway's side of the same interval is measured over real HTTP at 60 ms by tests/scale/replica-reconnect.scale.test.ts, see gateway.json), device flash I/O (node:sqlite in memory here, op-sqlite on flash there), and React render. So this is still a LOWER BOUND on what the owner feels. The ceiling is ~3.2x the slowest of four samples because a shared CI runner is materially slower than this host and four samples cannot bound its jitter; TIGHTEN further once ~10 nightly samples exist.

mountedReplicaReadWithOutbox.volume: 50,000 canonical document rows across 4 mounted vaults + 200 durable pending mutations (50 per vault)
mountedReplicaReadWithOutbox.probe: CENTRAID_PERF_EVIDENCE=1 bun run --cwd apps/mobile test -- src/lib/replica/multi-vault-reader.test.ts — production MultiVaultReplicaReader performs a 5,000-row ordered read and federated FTS search while enumerating and composing the durable SQLite outboxes

_provenance.host: macOS 26.2 arm64 development host, Node SQLite driver over the production reader/query plan
_provenance.note: MEASURED. The fixture includes the outbox volume in both timed requests; the read plan fetches the bounded canonical page plus only mutation-addressed canonical row ids.
_provenance.headroom: cold observed + 28%; search ceiling retained from the existing product budget

appWeight.volume: n/a — build artifact, independent of vault size
appWeight.probe: scripts/perf/app-weight.mjs --surface mobile (weighs dist/mobile-bundle-smoke/ios and .../android, both produced by the existing `bun run --cwd apps/mobile ci:bundle` in the ci.yml mobile-smoke job)

_provenance.host: darwin arm64, `bun run --cwd apps/mobile ci:bundle` (expo export, both platforms) in this worktree
_provenance.note: MEASURED. One ceiling covers both platforms because they differ by 7,750 B (0.07%). The Hermes bundle is 55% of the weight and the @expo/vector-icons font set is most of the rest — MaterialCommunityIcons.ttf alone is 1.31 MB and is the largest single asset. Ceilings are the larger observed value + ~8% headroom.
